data.title: DoE authorizes 400K-barrel emergency SPR release for Phillips 66 Lake Charles refinery
data.description:
The U.S. Department of Energy said Friday it authorized an emergency release of up to 400K barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.

"The supply will help offset temporary disruptions affecting crude oil deliveries to the refinery and support continued production of transportation fuels serving Louisiana and surrounding markets," the DoE said, without specifying the nature of the disruption at the 264K bbl/day refinery.

Phillips 66 confirmed it will receive crude from the SPR but did not comment on refinery operations or commercial activity except to say that "we do not anticipate impacts to Lake Charles ⁠operations."

Like most of the recent program of releases from the reserve, the DoE said it authorized release as an exchange, meaning Phillips 66 must return the same amount of oil it receives, along with additional barrels as a premium for the loan.

DoE data this week showed supplies in the reserve now total 282.7M barrels, its lowest level since October 1982, following drawdowns during the U.S.-Iran war and, earlier, Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

data.title: Top News Today:  Stocks Fall as Oil Climbs on Iran War Escalation Bets
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

STOCKS: Stocks fell as rising oil prices weighed on sentiment.

TREASURYS: Treasury yields rose as inflation concerns resurfaced ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting next week.

FOREX: The U.S. dollar strengthened ahead of the Fed meeting.

COMMODITIES: Oil futures rose by more than 3% in New York, blowing past the psychologically significant $100-a-barrel level, due to reports that the U.S. and Israel were weighing more attacks on Iran.

HEADLINES

American Express to Cut 3,500 Jobs

American Express is cutting 5% of its global workforce in an attempt

to put a cap on rising costs.

That reduction amounts to about 3,500 jobs, the company said Friday.

Chief Executive Stephen Squeri said the job reductions were part of a

plan to streamline the organization and invest in business priorities.

"We have got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over

the next few years, we needed to become a more agile and efficient

organization," Squeri said in a conference call with analysts.

Consumer Sentiment Declined Slightly in October

Consumer sentiment ticked slightly lower in October, hovering near

record-low levels, according to the end-of-month reading from the

University of Michigan's survey.

The survey's headline index came in at 48, versus 46.3 in the

preliminary October reading and down from 48.1 in September. It is the

final reading from the survey before November's midterm elections, with

voter frustration about the economy at the center of many campaigns.

Consumers' inflation expectations over both the near term and the long

term moved slightly higher.

SK Hynix Pauses IPO of Memory-Chip Unit as AI Valuation Fears Mount

SEOUL-SK Hynix has scrapped plans for a major U.S. public offering of

its flash-memory subsidiary Solidigm, highlighting deepening investor

caution toward artificial-intelligence valuations despite robust demand

for AI-related hardware.

The memory-chip maker, a key partner to Nvidia, said Friday that

market conditions and broader share-price trends drove the decision, and

that the move doesn't reflect any change in growth prospects for

Solidigm, which was formed after SK Hynix's acquisition of Intel's NAND

flash-memory business.

The Solidigm IPO would have raised funds for a new production facility

in the U.S. to meet rising demand, SK Hynix said.

Trump Expected to Remove Some Tariffs on Canada in Bid to Help Susan

Collins

The U.S. is expected to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian products

in a bid to help Sen. Susan Collins of Maine and other Republicans in the

upcoming midterm elections, according to people familiar with the

upcoming action.

The proclamation altering the tariffs, which could come as early as

Friday, will likely remove 50% tariffs on products used in agriculture,

according to the people, who emphasized that the scope and timing of the

action could change. The tariff reductions could be balanced out by

raising levies on other Canadian goods.

After The Wall Street Journal reported the expected action, Collins

issued a statement praising the Trump administration's move and further

detailing nine categories of tariff exemptions. They include certain

agricultural machinery, refrigeration equipment, packaging products and

other goods used in food production.

Bombardier to Invest $270 Million in U.S. Expansion as Trump Softens

Stance

Bombardier plans to invest $270 million to expand its American

infrastructure footprint and hire 800 U.S. workers, days after President

Trump appeared to soften his rhetoric against the Montreal-based

business-jet maker.

The expansion includes a significant step-up in operations in Texas,

opening a new service center in Indiana, building a learning hub in

Kansas, as well as launching additional infrastructure projects in

Connecticut.

In a Truth Social post at 11:41 P.M. Thursday, hours before

Bombardier's official announcement, Trump praised Bombardier's plans,

stating "Bombardier is investing 270 MILLION DOLLARS, creating THOUSANDS

of American Jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana."

Booz Allen Expects Growth to Accelerate as Civil Business Pressures Ease

Booz Allen Hamilton expects growth to accelerate in the second half of

its fiscal year, driven by continued demand for national-security

technologies and easing pressure in its civil business.

The trends gave the company confidence to raise its full-year earnings

outlook after reporting a higher profit in the latest quarter, even as

revenue declined due to continued weakness in its civil and commercial

business.

Booz Allen is currently operating in a split market, Chief Operating

Officer Kristine Martin Anderson said Friday on a call with analysts.

Rogers Communications Profit Drops on Comparison, Revenue Rises

Rogers Communications reported a decline in third-quarter profit due

to a large prior-year accounting gain tied to its sports assets

acquisition, while adjusted profit topped expectations on higher revenue.

The Canadian telecom company on Friday posted net income of 495

million Canadian dollars ($353.3 million), or C$0.88 a share, down from

C$5.77 billion, or C$10.54 a share, in the comparable quarter a year ago.

In the same period last year, Rogers booked a one-time, noncash paper

gain of C$5 billion when it revalued its existing stake in Maple Leaf

Sports & Entertainment, the parent company of the Toronto Maple Leafs and

Toronto Raptors, as part of its acquisition of Bell's ownership stake.

Archer to Launch Air Taxis in Texas

Archer Aviation plans to launch air taxi networks in three Texas

cities.

The electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft are slated to be

used for air-taxi services in Austin, Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth

area, the aircraft company said Friday.

Archer still requires approval from the Federal Aviation

Administration for its air taxi aircraft Midnight. It is in the final

stages of that regulatory process.

TALKING POINT Brokerage Firms Want to Yank Away Your Investor Protections

Should investors be protected from financial advisers, or should it be the other way around?

Regulators may soon decide whether an unlevel playing field should be tilted even more steeply against the little guy.

For years, arbitration has been the primary way individual investors can seek to recover losses caused by a broker or financial adviser. Investors usually don't prevail. At the largest securities-arbitration forum, run by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, which oversees the brokerage business, investors fail to win any damage awards in about three out of four cases that don't close in a settlement.

This March, Finra requested public comment on "modernizing" its arbitration rules. Outside analysts and attorneys expect proposed changes soon, perhaps by year-end.

Among the questions the regulator sought comment on: whether large or complex cases should go to arbitration forums not administered by Finra; whether punitive damages should be limited or precluded; and whether Finra's arbitration panels should include at least one member from the securities industry.

In early 2025, a Finra arbitration panel stunned the securities industry by ordering a unit of Stifel, the St. Louis-based brokerage and investment firm, to pay approximately $132 million, including punitive damages, to investors who claim to have been defrauded by a former Stifel financial adviser.

  • Jason Zweig, The Wall Street Journal

data.title: Dollar Tree, Dollar General Stocks Slide as Their Core Shoppers Get Squeezed — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

Shopper fatigue over rising prices might seem like a good thing for discount stores as more people hunt for bargains. But falling shares of Dollar Tree and Dollar General stores show the pressure on their core consumers.

The discounters' stocks both fell more than 6% Friday, before paring some of those losses by late afternoon. The declines placed them among the worst performers in the S&P 500 for the day. It's not just a one-day slump either: both stocks are roughly flat for the year.

Investors are "having concerns around the health of the consumer and rising oil costs after trading heavily into the retail sector yesterday, as higher oil prices can lead to higher inflation," Morningstar's Brett Husslein told Barron's. "We think investors were seeking a safe-haven that is reasonably insulated from AI-related themes yesterday and are now giving up those gains they saw the prior trading day."

While high prices can motivate more affluent shoppers to hunt for deals wherever they can find them, the chains' core consumers are being forced to pick and choose. Overall inflation combined with high fuel prices — oil futures are trading at five-month highs, while gas prices are up more than 40% since the Iran war started — hits lower-income shoppers harder because they have less discretionary income.

"That is forcing consumers, especially at the lower end of the income distribution, to deploy their purchasing power more consciously," PwC economists wrote in a recent report. "Consumers are still spending, but they are increasingly selective about where they spend and what they get in return," the report added.

While Dollar General's sales come mostly from consumables like shampoo and snacks, 18% come from more discretionary items like holiday decorations, picture frames and small appliances. By comparison, Dollar Tree gets just under half its revenue from consumables.

The worry is that the discounters' core shoppers will be forced to scale back on those discretionary purchases. Fewer than 40% of analysts covering either stock rate it Buy or Overweight.

Write to Anita Hamilton at anita.hamilton@barrons.com

data.title: U.S. Stocks See Further Downside, Dow Posts Steep Loss
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Following the sell-off seen during Thursday's session, stocks saw further downside over the course of the trading day on Friday. The major averages all ended the day in negative territory, with the Dow showing a particularly steep drop.

The Dow slumped 652.82 points or 1.2 percent to 52,215.16, pulling back off the one-month closing high set in the previous session.

The S&P 500 also fell 39.75 or 0.5 percent to a one-month closing low of 7,623.68, while the Nasdaq slipped 53.52 points or 0.2 percent to 25,955.34, ending the day at its lowest closing level since early August.

Despite the steep drop on the day, the Dow rose by 0.4 percent for the week, although the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted weekly losses of 0.5 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.

Lingering concerns about the artificial intelligence trade contributed to the weakness on Wall Street along with a continued increase in the price of crude oil.

U.S. crude oil futures have surged by more than 4 percent and jumped back well above $100 a barrel, while international benchmark Brent crude oil futures have reached a six-month high.

Concerns about supply disruptions in the Middle East continue to drive the price of crude oil higher amid continued attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthi militia of Yemen against Saudi Arabia.

Reports suggesting that the U.S. and Israeli are planning to renew military operations against Iran after the midterm elections have also contributed to the spike in crude oil prices.

However, traders seemed reluctant to make more significant moves ahead of several key events next week, including the Federal Reserve's latest monetary policy meeting.

The Fed is scheduled to announce its latest monetary policy decision next Wednesday, with the central bank widely expected to leave rates unchanged.

With a quarter point rate hike still widely expected at the Fed's December meeting, traders are likely to keep a close eye on the accompanying statement.

Earnings news is also likely to remain in the spotlight next week, with Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) among the companies due to report their quarterly results.

'A combination of measured central bank guidance and strong technology results could support a recovery in risk appetite, while hawkish policy signals and disappointing earnings could trigger another round of selling,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com.

'With U.S. GDP and PCE inflation also due, investors will have plenty of reasons to reassess interest rate expectations,' she added. 'The upcoming U.S. midterm elections on November 3 add another layer of uncertainty, suggesting volatility could remain elevated as markets head into November.'

Sector News

Airline stocks moved sharply lower amid the spike in crude oil prices, with the NYSE Arca Airline Index tumbling by 2.6 percent.

A steep drop by the price of gold also contributed to considerable weakness among gold stocks, as reflected by the 2.2 percent slump by the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index.

Pharmaceutical and retail stocks also notable weakness on the day, while oil service stocks surged along with the price of crude oil, resulting in a 5.5 percent spike by the Philadelphia Oil Service Index.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region turned in a mixed performance during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index dipped by 0.3 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index advanced by 0.9 percent.

Meanwhile, the major European markets all moved to the downside on the day. While the German DAX Index slid by 0.8 percent, the French CAC 40 Index and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index fell by 0.4 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively.

In the bond market, treasuries gave back ground after skyrocketing in the previous session. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, climbed 3.6 basis points to 4.988 percent.

data.title: TSX extends weekly decline as financials, consumer-related shares fall
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

Canada’s main stock index added to its weekly decline on Friday as losses for financials and consumer-related stocks offset gains for energy, with recent turbulence globally in AI-linked stocks keeping risk appetite in check.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended down 185.27 points, or 0.5%, at 35,788.18, its lowest closing level since October 14. For the week, the index was down 1.1%.

  • "It's been a risk-off week," said Greg Taylor, chief investment officer at PenderFund Capital Management.

  • "The TSX has held in better than some other indices for the last little bit," Taylor said. "It's probably been held up by the energy sector but we're starting to see some weakness in banks and some other parts of the market this week."

  • Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) fell 0.9% on Friday, with shares of Manulife Financial Corporation down 2.9%.

  • Food and pharmacy retailer Loblaws Companies lost 2.8%, contributing to a 2.2% decline for consumer staples.

  • The materials sector , which includes metal mining shares, fell 1.2% as gold hit a three-month low ahead of a Federal Reserve interest rate decision next week.

  • The Bank of Canada is also due to make an interest rate decision next week. The majority of economists polled by Reuters expect the central bank will raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% and follow with one more hike by the end of March.

  • Telecom operator Rogers Communications (RClb.TO) reported third-quarter profit above estimates. Still, its shares were down 2.3%.

  • Energy was the only one of 10 major sectors to end higher, adding 2.1%.

  • US crude oil futures settled 3.8% higher at $103.27 a barrel after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

  • US President Donald Trump signed an order to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products.

data.title: Summit Therapeutics and Lunit Announce Agreement to Apply AI-powered SCOPE IO Platform for Tumor Microenvironment Analysis in Immuno-Oncology Development
data.description:
Summit Therapeutics Inc. () and Lunit Inc. () today announced a research agreement to evaluate the use of Lunit SCOPE IO, Lunit’s AI-powered pathology platform, for tumor microenvironment analysis in support of Summit’s immuno-oncology development programs with ivonescimab.

The effort will focus on applying Lunit SCOPE IO to hematoxylin and eosin-stained (H&E) whole-slide images to characterize tumor microenvironment features. The companies aim to explore how AI-powered pathology analysis can support biomarker discovery, patient stratification or selection, and a deeper biological understanding of response to ivonescimab therapies.

Summit is developing ivonescimab, a novel, potential first-in-class investigational PD-1 / VEGF bispecific antibody, in several solid tumors. Lunit SCOPE IO is designed to support immuno-oncology research and biomarker development through AI-powered analysis of H&E slides, enabling scalable assessment of tumor microenvironment features without requiring additional stains or assays.

“Understanding the tumor microenvironment is increasingly important as immuno-oncology moves beyond single-axis checkpoint inhibition toward more complex mechanisms and combinations,” said Allen Yang, MD, PhD, Chief Research and Development Strategy Officer of Summit. “We are pleased to work with Lunit to explore how AI-powered pathology can help generate deeper, more scalable insights from routine tissue samples and inform the continued development of ivonescimab.”

“Summit is at the forefront of next-generation immuno-oncology development, and we are excited to support its efforts with Lunit SCOPE IO,” said Brandon Suh, Lunit CEO. “By extracting quantitative, spatially resolved immune and tumor microenvironment features from standard H&E slides, we believe SCOPE IO can help biopharma partners better understand which patients may benefit from immuno-oncology therapies and why.”

This agreement reflects the growing importance of computational pathology in oncology drug development. Routine H&E slides contain rich information about tumor architecture, immune infiltration, stromal organization, and spatial interactions within the tumor microenvironment. However, traditional manual assessment can be difficult to scale and may not fully capture the quantitative and spatial complexity of the tumor-immune interface. AI-powered analysis offers the potential to convert these routinely generated pathology images into reproducible, high-dimensional biomarker data.

The companies expect the work to generate tumor microenvironment insights that may inform future translational research, exploratory biomarker strategies, and clinical development planning. No clinical outcome data are being announced as part of this release.

Lunit SCOPE products are for research use only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures or decisions.

About Ivonescimab

Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit’s license territories, North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Japan, and as AK112 outside of Summit’s license territories, is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody combining the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects associated with blocking VEGF into a single molecule. By design, ivonescimab displays unique cooperative binding to each of its intended targets with multifold higher affinity to PD-1 when in the presence of VEGF.

This design is intended to differentiate ivonescimab as there is potentially higher expression (presence) of both PD-1 and VEGF in tumor tissue and the tumor microenvironment (TME) as compared to normal tissue in the body. Summit believes ivonescimab’s specifically engineered tetravalent structure (four binding sites) enables higher avidity (accumulated strength of multiple binding interactions) in the TME (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025). This tetravalent structure, the intentional novel design of the molecule, and bringing these two targets into a single bispecific antibody with cooperative binding qualities have the potential to direct ivonescimab to the tumor tissue versus healthy tissue. The intent of ivonescimab’s design, together with a half-life of 6 to 7 days after the first dose (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025) increasing to approximately 10 days at steady state dosing, is to improve upon previously established efficacy thresholds, side effects, and safety profiles associated with prior approved drugs to these targets.

Ivonescimab was invented by Akeso Inc. (HKEX Code: 9926.HK) and is currently utilized in multiple Phase III clinical trials. Over 5,000 patients have been treated with ivonescimab in clinical studies globally and over 100,000 patients when considering those treated in a commercial setting in China, as noted by Akeso.

There are currently 17 Phase III clinical studies that are either announced, ongoing, or have been completed studying ivonescimab, five of which are Summit-sponsored global studies, two of which are studies sponsored by cooperative groups, and 10 of which are being or have been conducted in China by Akeso. Summit began its clinical development of ivonescimab in NSCLC (HARMONi, HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7) and expanded its sponsored Phase III clinical development program into colorectal cancer (CRC; HARMONi-GI3) and urothelial carcinoma (bladder cancer; HARMONi-GU1). The two cooperative studies are in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC; ILLUMINE) and biliary tract cancer (BTC; EA2251).

Five Phase III ivonescimab clinical trials have read out to date, all five with positive data. Four of these five studies are in NSCLC and one is in BTC. In addition to Summit’s positive HARMONi study in NSCLC, Akeso has had positive read-outs in four single-region (China), randomized Phase III clinical trials, HARMONi-A, HARMONi-2, HARMONi-6 (each in NSCLC), and HARMONi-GI1 (in BTC) for ivonescimab, including a statistically significant overall survival benefit in all four studies from China.

Akeso is actively conducting additional Phase III clinical studies in settings outside of NSCLC and biliary-tract cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit’s license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024.

About Lunit Inc.

Founded in 2013, Lunit () is a global leader on a mission to conquer cancer through AI. Our clinically validated solutions span medical imaging, breast health, and biomarker analysis, empowering earlier detection, smarter treatment decisions, and more precise outcomes across the cancer care continuum.

Lunit offers a comprehensive suite spanning risk prediction and early detection to precision oncology. Our FDA-cleared Lunit INSIGHT Breast Suite and breast health solutions support cancer screening in thousands of medical institutions worldwide, while the Lunit SCOPE platform is used in research partnership with global pharma and laboratory leaders for biomarker research, and companion diagnostic development.

Trusted by over 10,000 sites in more than 65 countries, Lunit combines deep medical expertise with continuously evolving datasets to deliver measurable impact for patients, clinicians, and researchers alike. Headquartered in Seoul with global offices, Lunit is driving the worldwide fight against cancer. Learn more at lunit.io.

About Summit Therapeutics Inc.

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of patient-, physician-, caregiver- and societal-friendly medicinal therapies intended to improve quality of life, increase potential duration of life, and resolve serious unmet medical needs.

Summit was founded in 2003 and the company’s shares are listed on the Nasdaq Global Market (symbol "SMMT"). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, with additional offices in Palo Alto, California, Princeton, New Jersey, Dublin, Ireland, and Oxford, UK.

For more information, please visit https://www.smmttx.com and follow Summit on X @SMMT_TX.

data.title: Amy Johnson Appointed President of GDIT
data.description:
RESTON, Va., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- General Dynamics () announced today that Amy Johnson has been appointed as president of GDIT, effective November 3.

Johnson is a 27-year veteran of General Dynamics Mission Systems, where she held increasingly senior roles in engineering, engineering management and business leadership across cybersecurity, defense electronics, space and intelligence systems, most recently as vice president and general manager for Space, Cyber and Intelligence. She earned bachelor's and master's degrees in computer science and computer systems engineering.

"Amy has a proven track record of leading teams to solve complex and highly technical challenges for our customers," said Phebe Novakovic, CEO of General Dynamics. "I am confident that her dynamic leadership, operational rigor and deep commitment to our values and culture will deliver value to our customers, employees and shareholders."

GDIT delivers digital modernization, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and software development solutions to the U.S. federal government, defense, intelligence agencies and other customers. It is a business unit of General Dynamics, a global aerospace and defense company that offers a broad portfolio of products and services in business aviation; ship construction and repair; land combat vehicles, weapons systems and munitions; and technology products and services. General Dynamics employs more than 120,000 people worldwide and generated $52.6 billion in revenue in 2025. More information is available at gd.com.

TORONTO, ONTARIO – TheNewswire - October 23, 2026 - AEON STRATEGIES LTD. (formerly Cloud3 Ventures Inc.) (CSE: AEON) (OTCQB:CLDVF)(FSE:WQ40) (the “Company” or “Aeon”) announces that it expects to be unable to file its audited annual financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026, the related management’s discussion and analysis and the related CEO and CFO certifications (collectively, the “Annual Filings”) by the October 28, 2026 filing deadline under Part 4 of National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations and National Instrument 52-109 – Certification of Disclosure in Issuers’ Annual and Interim Filings. The delay is due to (i) the limited availability of the Company’s auditor, Davidson & Company LLP  (the “Auditor”); and (ii) the additional time required to complete audit procedures relating to the Company’s crypto-related investments, which are more complex than in prior years. The Auditor remains engaged, and the Company is working with the Auditor to complete the audit.

The Company has applied to the Ontario Securities Commission, as principal regulator, for a management cease trade order (the “MCTO”) under National Policy 12-203 – Management Cease Trade Orders (“NP 12-203”). If granted, the MCTO will prohibit the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer from trading in the Company’s securities until the Annual Filings are filed and the MCTO is revoked. The MCTO generally will not affect the ability of other shareholders to trade in the Company’s listed subordinate voting shares.

The Company currently expects to file the Annual Filings on or before December 4, 2026, and will issue a news release announcing the completion of such filings at that time. These guidelines require the Company to issue bi-weekly default status reports by way of news release for so long as the Annual Filings remain outstanding.

data.title: Wall Street closes lower to end rocky week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes: Dow down 1.23%, S&P 500 down 0.52%, Nasdaq down 0.21%
  • Telecom stocks fall after report of SpaceX wireless carrier talks
  • S&P 500 energy sector climbs, tracking jump in oil prices
  • Investors turn focus to big earnings week, Fed meeting

By Lewis Krauskopf, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Ragini Mathur

Wall Street's main indexes closed lower on Friday even as technology shares steadied somewhat to end a turbulent week for the market-driving AI trade, and investors looked ahead to a busy slate of corporate earnings and a Federal Reserve interest-rate policy meeting.

The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss a day after the tech-heavy index suffered its biggest one-day drop since June, as concerns flared over financing costs to support heavy AI investment spending. The S&P 500 technology sector posted a 0.35% gain on Friday.

Most S&P 500 sectors fell, however, including declines of well over 1% for the consumer staples and consumer discretionary groups as well as the financials sector.

Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies report quarterly results, including Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon , three AI hyperscalers whose capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

"There is still fallout from the questioning of the AI trade," said Kristina Hooper, chief market strategist at Man Group. "There's certainly the potential that we see less invested in an AI data center build-out next year than has been projected. So I certainly think that's giving pause."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16; the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 39.75 points, or 0.52%, to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 53.52 points, or 0.21%, to 25,955.34.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%. The blue-chip Dow rose 0.4%, its third straight weekly gain.

Telecommunications stocks fell, weighing on the communication services sector, after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier.

Shares of AT&T and T-Mobile both sank nearly 8% while Verizon shed 1.2%. SpaceX shares rose 1.9%. US cell tower operators gained, with Crown Castle up 9% and American Tower up 4%.

The energy sector rose 2.5%, hitting a record high. Brent crude hit its highest level since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

American Express shares fell 3.7%, weighing on the Dow. The company raised its profit forecast as it also announced plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce.

SLB shares rose 7% after the oilfield services provider beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit.

Data from the University of Michigan showed US consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October, as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with robust corporate profit growth underpinning gains for major equity indexes this year. S&P 500 companies are on track to have increased earnings by more than 32% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.

The Fed is expected to keep interest rates steady when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, but investors will be eager for clues about whether the US central bank will hike rates at its December meeting. Wall Street is also increasingly focused on the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.72-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. On the Nasdaq, declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.57-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 18 new 52-week highs and 8 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 74 new highs and 334 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 15.4 billion shares, compared with the 17.2 billion average over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Fall as Oil Prices Hit Five-Month High — Update
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Wall Street is continuing its move toward less risky investments, as oil prices climbed to their highest level in five months.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52215.16. The S&P 500 lost 39.75 points, or 0.52%, to 7623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 53.52 points, or 0.21%, to 25955.34.

Thursday's selloff of artificial intelligence-related stocks cooled down, allowing the tech-heavy Nasdaq to outperform. Treasury yields rebounded slightly after weathering their biggest one-day decline in more than three years.

The yield on the two-year Treasury gained 0.044 percentage point to 4.680%. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note rose 0.110 percentage point to 4.987% and the yield on the 30-year bond added 0.028 percentage point to 5.314%.

The Brent crude oil rose 3.1% to $116.72, its highest point since April, after Iran promised to retaliate if the U.S. and Israel restart their air strikes. Iran said it would respond with strikes not only on U.S. military bases, but also on airports, pipelines and civilian targets in the Persian Gulf. The energy sector led gains in the S&P 500 following the gains in oil.

Investors are continuing their move to less volatile stocks. So far this month, the consumer staples sector has climbed 9.6%, putting it on pace for its best month in 26 years. Other safe-haven sectors, including utilities and health care, are leading S&P 500 gains this month.

While shareholders fret over oil and tech, consumers are also less positive about the economy. The University of Michigan's monthly consumer-sentiment index showed Americans' mood ticked down in October, putting the metric at its lowest point heading into a major election.

Tech stock losses cooled, but concerns about high costs and barriers to AI growth haven't been completely assuaged. SK Hynix, a South Korean memory-chip maker, canceled its plans for a U.S. public offering, which was expected to fund its manufacturing expansion plans. Lam Research's stock flattened out Friday, but it is down 16% this week after sharing a disappointing outlook that it blamed on supply-chain constraints.

The ICE dollar Index edged higher, as most investors expect the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady at next week's meeting, though some are still anticipating a rate hike. Precious metals continued their decline, with gold falling 1.3% to $3,991.10 a troy ounce. Silver lost 1.9% to $53.711 a troy ounce, its lowest settlement since Nov. 26.

French protests have escalated, revolving around dissatisfaction with the cost of living and a widening budget deficit, while the government tries to pass a new fiscal budget.

American Express weighed on the Dow, with shares falling 3.7%. The credit-card company said it was cutting 5% of its workforce, or about 3,500 jobs, citing the need for a more streamlined business.

The energy conglomerate SLB closed up 7.1% after quarterly revenue rose, thanks to some recovery in the company's Middle East business. Expansion in North America, as well as growth in SLB's data-center business, also helped drive sales.

Deckers Outdoor, which makes Hoka and Ugg shoes, cut its sales outlook Thursday night, saying shoppers were getting more cautious. Waning demand for casual shoes is starting to bleed into the performance running sector. Deckers shares declined 4.9% and dragged down shares of rival sneaker companies, including On Holding and Nike.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Badger Meter 3Q 2026: Revenue $235.9M, Net income $35.9M, EPS $1.24— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Badger Meter reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $235.9 million, up 0.1% from a year earlier, while net income rose 2.4% to $35.9 million and diluted EPS increased 4.2% to $1.24. SaaS growth and higher ultrasonic meter volumes supported margin improvement.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $235.9M, compared with $235.7M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 0.1%.
  • Net income was $35.9M, compared with $35.1M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 2.4%.
  • Diluted EPS was $1.24, compared with $1.19 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 4.2%.

Business Highlights

  • Nine-month sales fell 5.1% to $660.5 million, primarily reflecting uneven timing of utility advanced metering infrastructure projects. Utility water accounted for about 89% of sales.
  • Flow instrumentation sales grew 2.1% in the quarter and 1.3% for the first nine months, supported by demand in water-focused markets.
  • Badger Meter added sewer-monitoring software provider UDlive to its utility water business in May 2026. The acquisition contributed $7.7 million in revenue through September.
  • Electronic-component shortages and tariffs could increase costs or disrupt supply. The company is pursuing alternate sourcing, inventory measures and pricing actions.

data.title: Aterian Secures Up to $1 Million in 8% Note Financing From Stockholder
data.description:
Aterian entered into an unsecured promissory note with stockholder Chen Zhipeng, who agreed to provide advances of up to $1 million. Advances accrue interest at 8% annually, and the note matures eight months after its October 20, 2026, date. Depending on specified conditions and the lender's election, amounts due may be repaid in cash or applied to a future private placement or converted into common stock, subject to Nasdaq issuance limits and required approvals.

Agreement details:

  • Agreement type: Unsecured promissory note
  • Counterparty: Chen Zhipeng
  • Signed / Effective: Oct 20 2026 / same
  • Duration / Termination: 8 months
  • Reason: Provide access to funding for approved company uses

Original SEC Filing: Aterian, Inc. [ ATER ] - 8-K - Oct. 23, 2026

data.title: AEON Biopharma Outlines ABP-450 Biosimilar Plan, Targets Q4 2026 IND
data.description:
AEON Biopharma outlined its plan to develop ABP-450 as a potential biosimilar to BOTOX®, with a CMAP study IND submission planned for Q4 2026.

Key Highlights:

  • AEON is pursuing a 351(k) biosimilar pathway and targeting full-label access across BOTOX®’s 12 therapeutic indications.
  • FDA feedback indicated previously completed comparative studies may be submitted as supportive evidence with appropriate scientific bridging.
  • The proposed CMAP pharmacodynamic study is designed to compare ABP-450 and BOTOX®; study initiation is expected in Q1 2027.
  • ABP-450 has not been FDA-approved for any therapeutic indication; its safety and effectiveness for therapeutic use have not been established.

Original SEC Filing: AEON Biopharma, Inc. [ AEON ] - 8-K - Oct. 23, 2026
